page.overview:
Who is Emerson Fittipaldi?

Emerson Fittipaldi ( ; born December 12, 1946, in São Paulo, Brazil) is a Brazilian racing driver who won two Formula One World Drivers' Championships in and , and was also very successful racing in America, becoming a two-time winner of the Indianapolis 500 and winning the CART series in 1989.

Almost instantly promoted to lead driver of the team in , Fittipaldi won the championship in with one of F1's best ever cars, the Lotus 72D. Fittipaldi joined in , and won the championship that season. In , he moved to his brother Wilson's team, where he stayed until he exited the sport after without further success.

After retiring from F1, and largely not driving for three years, he received an offer to drive the CART series in the US. He competed in the US for another 12 years.

He is the brother of Wilson Fittipaldi, uncle of Christian Fittipaldi, and grandfather of Pietro Fittipaldi.
